money_at_stake.rationale: Sized on the annual value of the US sector the pathogen is actually inside, from the official series, rather than on the disaster's global reach or on any multiplier. USDA ERS puts total US poultry sector sales at $81.7 billion in 2025, up from $70.3 billion in 2024, with broilers at $44.6 billion. That single national sector already sits well inside B10_100 on its own, and the pathogen is in all of it: the Farm Bureau reads the same outbreak as 127 million egg layers lost since 2022, an average of 42.3 million per year, about 11% of the 5-year average annual layer inventory of 383 million hens. The federal response is a second, independent read that lands in the same place from below: $1 billion committed to the HPAI strategy and $1.46 billion already paid out in indemnity. Deliberately NOT used to size this leg: the industry's own $663,644,111,500 annual economic-impact figure, which is a multiplier claim over jobs and wages rather than a pool anyone can win, and the global sector, which no source on disk prices. GT_100B would require the global food chain and the human-pandemic tail, and neither is cited here, so the band stops at B10_100.

public_reach.rationale: This is the leg that inverts the occurrence, and it is scored low on a specific structural fact rather than on a feeling about agriculture. The two tightest points on this chain are not listed anywhere. All of the world's layer and turkey breeding stock and most of its broiler stock originates from two private companies, EW Group of Germany and Hendrix Genetics of the Netherlands; EW Group describes itself as a family holding company with more than 300 subsidiaries, in its third generation. The same EW Group owns VALO BioMedia, which its own site describes as the home for all SPF and Clean Egg activities of the group, and specific-pathogen-free eggs are the substrate egg-based human influenza vaccines are grown in. The other SPF leader was inside a listed issuer and left: Charles River sold Avian Vaccine Services, which supplies specific-pathogen-free chicken eggs and chickens, to a private investor group for approximately $170 million, agreed 2022-11-01. So at both the genetic origin and the vaccine substrate, a listed investor cannot buy the scarcity at any price. Not scored lower because real listed exposure does exist further down: animal-health vaccines, diagnostics, layer and broiler production, egg processing and rendering all have listed names, and Post's Michael Foods segment is a large egg-products business inside a listed issuer. Scored at 32 rather than 50 because that listed exposure sits in the diluted middle where the pathogen is a line item, not the business, and it is exactly where the taxpayer, not the shareholder, absorbs the loss. AMENDED 2026-09-11 after the census. This leg originally said a listed investor cannot buy the scarcity at either choke point. That is still true at the SPF egg link and it is NOT true at the genetics link: Cobb-Vantress, one of the three primary broiler breeders, is named in Tyson Foods' own Exhibit 21 subsidiary list, so one listed route exists. The score is left at 32 rather than raised, and the reason is stated rather than assumed: the route is a subsidiary among hundreds inside a protein processor, which is dilution rather than access, and the layer and turkey genetics that the egg side of this occurrence actually runs on remain with two private groups. A reader who disagrees with leaving the score unchanged has the fact and can re-score it.

capture_odds.rationale: Scored below the midpoint because on this chain the loss is socialised and the gain is competed away, and both halves are cited. On the loss side, APHIS pays producers the market value of destroyed birds: the programme has paid $1.46 billion, and the fourth-largest recipient is a listed egg producer. A shareholder therefore neither bears the full downside nor keeps a scarcity rent that the public is funding. On the gain side, the one link that could hold durable pricing power against the outbreak, animal-health vaccination, cannot deploy on commercial judgment at all: Zoetis has held a USDA conditional license for an H5N2 killed-virus vaccine since February 2025, and the decision to vaccinate commercial poultry flocks rests solely with national regulatory authorities in partnership with the poultry industry, held back by export-trade risk rather than by efficacy. A revenue line whose start date is a trade negotiation is not a capturable margin until that negotiation ends. Not scored lower because two links genuinely do capture: the private genetics duopoly captures completely, which is precisely why the public_reach leg is 32, and the depopulation and disposal link is paid to do work that only rises with the outbreak. Scored at 38, just under the REACHABLE threshold, and the appraisal states plainly that a USDA vaccination authorisation would be the single event that lifts this leg.

timing_fit.rationale: The money moves well inside the 2 to 5 year window and part of it has already moved twice. The outbreak is not a forecast: the virus was detected in 28 U.S. states in the first weeks of 2026 alone, and the same series shows the egg price cycle completing a full round trip inside the window, which is what a repeating supply shock looks like rather than a one-off. The commercial fuse is dated but not yet lit: the USDA is developing a formal national poultry vaccination plan and under the draft any flock testing positive would still be culled even if vaccinated, a policy meant to reassure trading partners, so the decision is live and the chain reprices when it lands. Held at 72 rather than higher because the single largest re-rating event, that vaccination authorisation, has now been pending since 2025 with no announced date, and an occurrence whose fuse has already slipped a year can slip another. The ecological leg of the occurrence runs faster than the commercial one and pulls the score up rather than down: Australia went from clean to 498 animals across six states inside three to four months.

notes.text: LEAKY is not a disappointment here, it is the answer. The band falls out of reach being under 60 while the money band is B10_100, which is the exact shape method section 0.2 defines LEAKY to catch: a large pool that does not land on listed issuers. On this occurrence it is structural rather than incidental, because the scarcity sits inside two private holdings and a private-equity carve-out, and because the taxpayer indemnifies the listed link's losses at market value. A chain build is still worth doing on a LEAKY occurrence of this size, and Ron commissioned one; what LEAKY says is that the chain should be read for where the exposure is diluted, not for where it is concentrated.
